import hashlib
import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

protocol = json.loads(Path('/tmp/tbp-follow-up-protocol.json').read_text())
base = Path('/tmp/tbp-good-pr-base-probe')
candidate = Path('/tmp/tbp-good-pr-probe')
summary = Path('evals/results/visual-evidence-gpt-5.4.json')
results = []

def run(name, root, historical=False, mutation=None):
    path, altered = mutation if mutation else (None, None)
    original = path.read_bytes() if path else None
    command = ['python3', 'scripts/build_eval_evidence.py', 'verify']
    if historical:
        command.append('--historical')
    command.append(str(summary))
    try:
        if path:
            path.write_bytes(altered)
        completed = subprocess.run(command, cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True)
        expected = next(check for check in protocol['checks'] if check[0] == name)
        result = {
            'case': name, 'source_revision': protocol['base' if root == base else 'candidate'],
            'command': command, 'exit_code': completed.returncode,
            'stdout': completed.stdout, 'stderr': completed.stderr,
            'meets_expectation': completed.returncode == expected[1]
                and expected[2] in completed.stdout + completed.stderr,
        }
        if path:
            result['mutation'] = {
                'path': str(path.relative_to(root)),
                'original_sha256': hashlib.sha256(original).hexdigest(),
                'altered_sha256': hashlib.sha256(altered).hexdigest(),
                'operation': 'replace first aggregate rate with -1' if name.endswith('statistic')
                    else 'append newline and a probe comment' if 'prose' in name
                    else 'append newline',
            }
        results.append(result)
    finally:
        if path:
            path.write_bytes(original)

run('base-clean', base)
p = base / 'skills/good-pr/SKILL.md'
run('base-later-prose-edit', base, mutation=(p, p.read_bytes() + b'\n<!-- one-off later prose edit -->\n'))
run('candidate-default', candidate)
run('candidate-historical', candidate, historical=True)
p = candidate / 'skills/good-pr/SKILL.md'
run('candidate-historical-later-prose-edit', candidate, historical=True,
    mutation=(p, p.read_bytes() + b'\n<!-- one-off later prose edit -->\n'))
for case, relative in [
    ('corrupt-output', 'evals/results/visual-evidence-gpt-5.4-outputs.jsonl'),
    ('corrupt-manifest', 'evals/visual-evidence-benchmark.json'),
    ('corrupt-baseline', 'evals/baselines/good-pr-8e613be/SKILL.md'),
]:
    p = candidate / relative
    run('candidate-historical-' + case, candidate, historical=True,
        mutation=(p, p.read_bytes() + b'\n'))
p = candidate / summary
data = json.loads(p.read_text())
data['final_frozen_run']['old_skill']['objective_pass_rate'] = -1
run('candidate-historical-forged-statistic', candidate, historical=True,
    mutation=(p, (json.dumps(data, indent=2) + '\n').encode()))
record = {
    'protocol': protocol,
    'results': results,
    'implementation': Path(__file__).read_text(),
    'working_trees_restored': all(not subprocess.run(
        ['git', 'status', '--porcelain'], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True,
        check=True).stdout for root in [base, candidate]),
}
Path('/tmp/tbp-follow-up-results.json').write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + '\n')
for result in results:
    print(result['case'], 'PASS' if result['meets_expectation'] else 'FAIL',
          result['exit_code'], (result['stdout'] + result['stderr']).strip().splitlines()[-1])
assert all(result['meets_expectation'] for result in results)
assert record['working_trees_restored']

K87.title: Add envelope v2 authoring: UI, MCP, notation, and verification
K87.body:
## What and why

Add envelope-v2 authoring on the runtime foundation already merged in #116 and
timing stack #107–#114: capability-aware exact editing, atomic XY transactions,
MCP authoring/read/analysis, and notation v2.4 with executable examples.
This PR does not replace the scheduler, readiness state machine, output graph,
or renderer-migration authorities.

## Rebase — 2026-10-19

Rebased onto main `869d3f5095084003e1251aa3ebf2eab8f65f62fe`. Previous PR head
`bdf9bae25e6b13e635dd0d368e2447a3f23118b7` is retained locally as
`backup/pr87-before-20261019`; its October 3 CI completed successfully.

Main now includes #122, incorporating the work from closed PRs #123/#126, plus
#128's patched dependency trees. Their three Vitest projects, shared audit
fixtures, bounded retries, fail-closed audio checks, and lockfiles are preserved.
The sole textual rebase conflict was Lessons Learned: main's Lesson 83 is kept
and the earlier authoring-ownership lesson is numbered 84. No new product/audio
behavior was introduced by this rebase. Spec status and historical receipts
are explicitly dated.

## Verification

Fresh local macOS / Node 26 verification (CI uses Node 24):

- Product unit lane: **4,938 passed**, one existing environment-gated skip.
- Audio-render lane: **26 passed**; verification-tooling lane: **117 passed**.
- Real built Worker integration: **131 passed**.
- Real local Worker browser lane: **77 passed**, zero skips/retries and exact
  identity gate pass, including authored-envelope convergence and reload.
- Editor contract: **3 passed**; editor-disabled runtime/notation: **1 passed**;
  both exact-identity gates pass with zero helper retries.
- App build/TypeScript, lint, Worker typecheck/dry-run bundle: pass.
- Documentation/examples, resource budgets, all test-quality checks, manifests,
  and exact E2E inventories: pass; every one of 375 test files has a lane.
- All three lockfile-pinned dependency installs report zero known vulnerabilities.

New-head GitHub CI is running. Do not
reuse the October 3 green CI run as evidence for this new head. No retries,
skips, timeout increases or hook bypasses were added to make checks pass.

## Costs and limits

Fresh same-toolchain builds against current main reproduce these measurements:

| Gzipped JavaScript | Main | Candidate | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Initial graph | 227,479 B | 227,841 B | +362 B (+0.16%) |
| All chunks | 313,121 B | 326,516 B | +13,395 B (+4.28%) |
| Lazy sequencer/editor | 29,787 B | 38,467 B | +8,680 B (+29.14%) |

Notation is a separate lazy 4,337 B gzip chunk. The audio catalogue remains
582 files / 42,914,625 encoded bytes with the same content hash. Worker bundle:
2,030,691 JS bytes, 3,506,127 uploaded bytes, within the explicit ratchet.
Both builds retain the existing >500 kB main-chunk warning. Browser heap and
decoded-memory deltas are not measured; unchanged assets do not prove unchanged
UI heap. These local runs do not establish CI p50/p95 or production readiness.

## Integration and remaining work

- #127's piano-roll dock conflicts with this branch in the track row, parameter
  editor, pattern-tools panel, sequencer wiring, row regression, and lane
  contracts. Headless MCP/notation is a useful first review unit; envelope UI
  should integrate with the chosen dock, not become a competing row layout.
- #130 is #127's green harness prerequisite and its authority is pinned to
  current main. Review it before another merge moves that base.
- D2 Summary → Shape → Details, recipes, track-local Start/Tail, selected-track
  phase audition, and labelling/hiding unsynced global synth macros remain.
- Renderer promotion still requires independent real advanced-renderer PCM,
  listening approvals, canary/rollback, and one release cycle. All 32 native
  presets retain their native route. Additional loop/release assets and nonzero
  loop crossfade remain separately gated; no new assets are promoted.
- #75 mute/solo ownership, #106 source certification, and #115 Safari background
  policy remain separate unresolved acceptance work.

This remains a broad authoring candidate, not a completed ADSR overhaul or a
renderer cutover. No merge or deployment is performed by this rebase.

## Visual evidence

The rebase changes no authoring pixels relative to the previous PR head; main
does not yet have this exact editor. Retained historical image: inspect the AHD
capability summary and Trigger/Gate choice. It is not a new-head screenshot and
does not prove beginner usability, audible equivalence, or mobile memory.

![Historical exact AHD editor with its capability summary and Trigger/Gate controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adewale/keyboardia/0fb06b66e9d0516c7ee4f661b61dfd3e1966e822/artifacts/envelope-v2-current-desktop.jpg)

Reproduce current controls: `cd app && npm run test:e2e:envelope`. Current browser
contracts independently cover the capability controls and portrait/landscape
exposure; product/multiplayer tests cover transactional state behavior.

K127.title: feat: piano roll editor dock, with spec, mocks and a first implementation
K127.body:
## What changed

This PR now carries the piano roll editor dock in three layers, which are at different points:

- **Spec** (`specs/PIANO-ROLL-DOCK.md`): the current design. Rows on a 36 × 50 cell lattice at a 53px pitch; a 231px control tile with the track (name over M S) on the left and the pattern ([Notes | Lane | Tools] over [Copy | Clear | Delete], transpose and steps beside) on the right; production's naming rule; lock marks (level fill, pitch badge, tie bridge, envelope fold, dashed kept lock); Lucide icons; one button language (solid commands, hollow state boxes that fill light when on, bare-text information); the roll opening at 18px per semitone; a copy status line in the transport; the name keeping production's click-to-preview and double-click rename.
- **Interactive mock** (`specs/mocks/piano-roll-dock.html`): implements that design end to end.
- **App implementation** (`app/`): an earlier phase of the design. `PianoRollEditor` and the editor dock under the grid with detents and ghosts; the loop ruler in the grid on shared step geometry (`step-geometry.ts`); Step and Track panes; the landscape bottom dock; a two-line control block at 134px; the SVG pitch contour overlay, the mobile edit panel, `InlineDrawer` and the dock's Grid view retired; row Copy, Clear and Delete moved into the Track pane.
- **Grid alignment fix** (84cee834): `.tracks-inner` is inline-flex, so it sat on its first item's baseline. Once the loop ruler row became that first item, the whole grid dropped 2.25px and every cell landed on a quarter pixel (the 36×37 step-cell and 49px velocity-lane captures). `vertical-align: top` restores it.
- **Visual baselines** (585ab334): regenerated on the CI image by `visual-baselines.yml` (run 39162664986) and reviewed image by image. Four intended changes: the ruler inside the scroller with its "Loop" label (sequencer-grid, tablet, desktop-wide), and the velocity lane at 1184px because the control column is 134px.

The implementation does not yet follow the latest spec: tile F at 231px with actions in the tile, the 36 × 50 lattice, the new lock marks in place of in-cell pitch contour marks, Lucide icons and the light on-state are still to do.

This branch is rebased onto `main` at `869d3f50`. The rebase preserves the previous PR head's file tree, including main's Lesson 83 and this branch's Lessons 84 and 85.

## Why

Keep sequencer rows contiguous while giving every track Track and Step editing and melodic tracks a Notes view, without panels opening between rows.

## Verification

- Pre-push T0 on each push: manifests, E2E inventories and unit tests.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run validate:test-quality` passed locally on 84cee834.
- Grid fix: the loop-ruler placement test in `e2e/piano-roll-dock.spec.ts` asserts the ruler row starts at the scroller's top edge. 41 tests across the dock, landscape-alignment, velocity-lane, pitch-contour and scrollbar specs pass with the fix.
- CI on 585ab334: every lane green, including E2E Visual Regression, except Stack A Identity (see Risk).
- The mock was exercised in headless Chromium: tile geometry, pane switching, copy/paste/cancel status, name preview vs double-click rename, roll sizing; no page errors.

- [x] If this fixes a bug, the regression test fails when the fix is reverted or disabled (or the description explains why that control is impractical). Control for the grid fix: with `vertical-align: top` removed, the loop-ruler test fails with `Expected: 0, Received: 2.25`.

## Risk

The app code reflects an older phase of the design than the spec and mock, so reviewing the implementation against the spec will show deliberate gaps. Open decisions recorded in the spec: amending `specs/ICON-SYSTEM.md` for icon-only Copy/Clear/Delete, and a resting treatment that tells Delete from Clear.

**Stack A Identity is red and needs a maintainer decision.** The gate requires head to render identically to the merge base, and this redesign removes the row's step-count dropdown and changes the row's DOM. Its protected harness can only change through a prerequisite PR or a one-time merge-base exception. Details are in the PR comment.

comments.body:
**Stack A Identity is red by design on this PR, and it needs a maintainer decision.**

The gate requires head to render identically to the merge base. This PR redesigns the track row, so it can't:

- **Stack B full-app `*-step-open` (6 states):** they time out waiting for `.track-row .step-count-trigger`. The redesign removed the step-count dropdown from the row, so the element no longer exists.
- **Stack B `full-app-landscape-*-unaffected` (3):** the accessibility tree differs because the row's DOM changed (two-line control block, pitch-editor toggle). This is intended.
- **Stack A `desktop-integrated-fx-*` (3):** in the catalogue, `.swing-value` in the transport changed from cyan monospace 11px to yellow 14px. The catalogue imports only `TrackRow.css`, and this PR moved the pattern-tools rules (including a global `.swing-value`) to `PatternToolsPanel.css`. In the production bundle the transport swing value is unchanged: the rule order is the same in both builds.

`serve-stack-a-comparison.mjs` protects the harness files and refuses edits to them unless `STACK_A_ALLOW_HARNESS_CHANGES=1`. A fix from inside this PR would weaken the gate, so I haven't touched it. The two routes the README and history support:

1. A prerequisite harness PR: drop or re-target the step-count full-app states, re-record the landscape states, and have the catalogue import `PatternToolsPanel.css`.
2. A one-time merge-base exception for this PR, as used for the Stack B pilot and the colour-role migration.

The other failures on this PR are addressed. 84cee834 fixes the 2.25px grid offset behind the step-cell, velocity-lane and sample-picker drifts; the regression check fails with "Received: 2.25" when the fix is reverted. 585ab334 adds the CI-rendered baselines for the intended grid changes.

G18.title: Check retired-tool callers and scope PR verification claims
G18.body:
Deleting a validator can leave package scripts and contributor instructions calling a missing file. A later follow-up push can also leave a PR claiming that older checks passed at the new head. Add explicit review guidance and tune scenarios for both failures.

The existing proof verifier exposed the same evidence-scope problem: it requires today's skill tree to match an archived model run, so any subsequent skill edit fails that CI step. Add an explicit `verify --historical` mode for CI that still checks recorded source trees, artifact hashes, baseline bytes, regraded outputs, and canonical statistics. Its output states that the archive does not evaluate the current skill. Default verification and bundle building retain the clean, matching current-skill requirement. Preserve the archived results unchanged and update the affected ablation patch offsets.

Validation: all 44 unit tests, install-boundary, Ruff, both pinned Harness 0.6.0 manifests, strict leakage/ablation checks, blocker audit, and historical verification of all 81 archived outputs passed locally. Tests cover default rejection of a changed skill, archive-only scope, and corrupt-artifact rejection. No new model comparison was run; the historical run is not evidence of improved behavior at this head.

**E2E Tests (mock API), (offline functional), (PCM capture) and (real backend) failed on 5f17f63b, and the cause is not this PR's.**

All four died at `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`, before any test ran:

```
Runner Image: ubuntu-26.04 (20261025.179.1)
BEWARE: your OS is not officially supported by Playwright; installing dependencies for ubuntu26.04-x64 as a fallback.
Cannot install dependencies for ubuntu26.04-x64 with Playwright 1.57.0!
Error: ERROR: Playwright does not support chromium on ubuntu26.04-x64
```

GitHub moved `ubuntu-latest` to Ubuntu 26.04. Ten Playwright jobs in `ci.yml` float on `ubuntu-latest`: instrument-validation, e2e-tests, e2e-offline-functional, e2e-offline-audio, e2e-pcm, e2e-real-backend, e2e-real-backend-webkit, e2e-mobile-safari and e2e-visual. Only `stack-a-identity` is pinned to `ubuntu-24.04`. Every PR and main will hit this until CI changes; a re-run lands on the same image. No fix exists on main yet (still 869d3f50).

Proposed patch, a separate CI PR rather than widening this one:

- Pin those jobs to `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04`, as `stack-a-identity` already is.
- Pin the regenerate job in `visual-baselines.yml` the same way. The committed Linux baselines were rendered on 24.04, and a 26.04 runner would also change font rasterisation.
- Moving to 26.04 later means a Playwright release that supports it plus regenerated visual baselines.

**Stack A Identity failed on f925c5ee: `step-count-open-width-768`, 1761 pixels outside the targets. This time the attached captures show what changed.**

That is the same state and the same pixel count as the failure on 68430e6c. The before/after/diff images attached by 0c9ee7fa locate it:

- Every differing pixel is text inside the open step-count menu (x 101–178, y 180–445). Backgrounds, borders and every element's rect are identical, and the ink totals are identical.
- In each unselected row, the grey secondary label (`¼ bar`, `2 bars`, `triplet`…) is drawn **exactly 1px higher** on head than on base, while the white value next to it doesn't move. In the selected row it's the reverse: the label stays and `16` moves up 1px.

So the same glyphs snap to a different whole pixel with identical geometry. My leading hypothesis, not yet proven:

- The menu's 150ms `dropdown-appear` animation (`translateY(-4px)` → 0) can give it its own compositing layer.
- Text on that layer snaps against the layer's grid instead of the page's, so the result depends on whether the layer still exists when the screenshot rasterises.
- The state started failing only after 68430e6c, which finishes animations right after each action. It failed 2 of the 3 CI runs since, and passed 20 local repeats plus 75 local runs under load on an older Chromium (1194, against CI's 1200).

Options, none pushed while the branch is being edited:

1. **Cancel instead of finish** the finished, non-filled animations in the capture's settle step, then wait two frames, so no animation layer can survive into the screenshot.
2. **Revert the Stack B half of 68430e6c** and fix `transpose-option-hover` by settling only that state's hover target.
3. **Snap `.dropdown-menu`'s fixed `top` to whole pixels in product code.** Most direct, but a product change, so it belongs in its own PR before this one.

I'd try (1) first and confirm it over repeated CI runs, since the race only shows on CI.

**Stack A Identity failed on deb5ae3 before any test ran: the one-time harness authority has expired.**

```
Error: Protected Stack A identity files differ from the merge base. Land harness changes as a prerequisite with STACK_A_ALLOW_HARNESS_CHANGES=1.
```

`serve-stack-a-comparison.mjs` authorises this PR's harness edits only while the merge base is `869d3f5095084003e1251aa3ebf2eab8f65f62fe`. Merging main (119fc84) moved it to `90ecc152330cabc33060788f14c67795307d4bba` (#132), so the exception no longer applies. This is the expiry the PR's Risk section describes, not a regression.

The fix is one line, the same deliberate update the earlier exceptions needed:

```js
const catalogueReviewBaseSha = '90ecc152330cabc33060788f14c67795307d4bba';
```

It expires again if main moves before this merges. I haven't pushed it, because this PR is in draft and being edited.

The runner-image failures from 1 November are gone: #132 pins every Linux job to `ubuntu-24.04`.

**Pushed d4087f94: renews the authority for base `90ecc152` and fixes the `step-count-open-width-768` race.** This corrects my earlier recommendation.

The race reproduced locally on Chromium 1243, which let me probe it. The step-count menu sits at `top: 138.5px`, so its text can snap to either pixel. Over 30 opens at 768×1024:

| Settle step after the click | Distinct label rasters |
|---|---|
| `finish()` (68430e6c) | 2 (29 / 1) |
| `cancel()` (my earlier option 1) | 2 (29 / 1) |
| let the animation end on its own | 1 (30 / 30) |
| `await animation.finished` | 1 (60 / 60, the same raster) |

So cancelling would not have fixed it. Both specs now await each finite animation's `finished` promise. Hovering still waits for the menu to stop moving, so `transpose-option-hover` stays fixed.

Locally against 90ecc152: eight consecutive full identity runs, 47/47 Chromium tests each, against a baseline of one failure in four runs. `validate:stack-b-evidence` passes with full history; on a shallow clone your ancestry check can't run, but CI's Stack A job fetches with depth 0.
